control_failures.control_label: secondary containment by bund and drainage
restraint and placarding of transported loads
selection, fit testing and maintenance of respirators

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: chemical release during commissioning of replacement equipment on P-8303

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control BUND_AND_DRAINAGE_CONTAINMENT: the secondary containment by bund and drainage was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control EXPOSURE_MONITORING: the monitoring of airborne contaminant exposure had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as an individual or team action.

Control LOAD_RESTRAINT_AND_PLACARDING: the restraint and placarding of transported loads had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.

Control RESPIRATORY_PROTECTION_PROGRAM: the selection, fit testing and maintenance of respirators was never verified as effective, and the root cause analysis classified this as an organisational factor.

recommendations: Restore the secondary containment by bund and drainage on P-8303 and TK-8311 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in controlling airborne contaminants, specifically selecting, fit-testing and maintaining respirators. P-8303 (reagent dosing pumps) is in service for reagent make-up and dosing. The task proceeded during commissioning of replacement equipment while the secondary containment by bund and drainage was never verified as effective. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 11 March 2015 an incident occurred on P-8303 and TK-8311 at Tolgarra Processing and Power Station during commissioning of replacement equipment, releasing chemical energy held as hydrocarbon.
